title: CheckoutScenarioInput
description:
A named setup of the local checkout: a file of `checkouts/`. It sets what a checkout
depends on on top of the store data, and what it does not set stays as the store data says.

$schema.description:
Lets editors validate and autocomplete the file, e.g.
`"../schema/checkout-scenario.schema.json"`.

title.description: The name shown on the home page. Defaults to the name of the file.

description.description: What the scenario is for and what to look at, shown on the home page.

session.description:
Who buys and what is in the cart, written as the `session` of the store data and applied
on top of it: `customer`, `cart` (lines, quantities, selling plans, note, attributes),
`country`, `company_location`.

entered.description: What the buyer already entered: email, address, discount codes, delivery and payment.

language.description:
The language of the buyer, by ISO code (`"fr"`): one of `localization.languages`. The
checkout opens under its locale root. Defaults to the primary language.

checkout.description:
Overrides of the `checkout` section of the store data: every field that is present
replaces the one of the store (`shipping_rates`, `payment_methods`, `discounts`,
`tax_rate`), except `functions` and `extensions`, which replace the settings of the
Functions and extensions they name.

variant.description: The look of the page. Defaults to the one of the server (`--variant`).

extensions.description:
The handles of the extensions (Functions and checkout UI extensions) that run, among
those of the app that `--extension` allows. When omitted, every UI extension shows and the
Functions run as at the shop's checkout: a payment or delivery customization, validation or
cart transform Function only through an enabled owner of it.

expect.description:
What the checkout must look like once the Functions ran: `lsf app check` fails when it
does not, and says what it expected and what it got. Without it, `app check` only checks
that the Functions run without an error.

SessionInput.description:
The state a browser session starts with. Tests can replace it per session through the
control API (`PUT /__lsf/session`).

$schema.description: Lets editors validate and autocomplete the file, e.g. `"../schema/session.schema.json"`.

customer.description:
Who is logged in: the email of a customer, `"default"` for the first customer of the
data, or `"none"`. Nobody is logged in when omitted.

cart.description: The content of the cart. Empty when omitted.

country.description:
ISO code of the selected country. When omitted, the visitor is in the shop's country
(`shop.address.country_code`), the one of its primary market: the storefront shows it,
and the checkout, until an address is entered, is in it (its Functions, its UI extensions
and its address form read it). A shop in a country the store does not sell to uses the
first country.

company_location.description:
For a B2B customer: the name of the company location they buy for. Defaults to the
first one they have access to.

CartInput.description: The cart a session starts with.

CartLineInput.description: A line of the cart a session starts with.

variant.description: A variant, by id or SKU, or a product handle (its first variant is used).

selling_plan.description:
The selling plan the line is bought with: its name or its id. The product of the
variant must be sold with it.

VariantRef.description:
A reference to a variant: its numeric id, its SKU, or a product handle (meaning that
product's first variant).

SellingPlanRef.description: A reference to a selling plan: its numeric id, or its name.

ScenarioEnteredInput.description: What the buyer already typed and chose when a scenario opens.

email.description: The contact email. A logged-in customer has theirs already.

shipping_address.description: The delivery address. Its country is the country of the checkout.

delivery.description:
The handle of the shipping rate chosen (`checkout.shipping_rates`). The first one
available is chosen when omitted.

payment.description: The handle of the payment method chosen (`checkout.payment_methods`).

discount_codes.description:
The discount codes entered, in order. A code that no discount of `checkout.discounts`
has is entered all the same, and refused as on Shopify.

ScenarioAddressInput.description: A postal address the buyer already entered.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of one of the store's countries: `"US"`.

CheckoutInput.description: How the local checkout (`lsf app dev --app`) is set up. Every field has a default.

shipping_rates.description: The delivery options offered to every address. Defaults to one, "Standard" at 5.00.

payment_methods.description: The payment methods. Defaults to "Credit card", "Cash on Delivery" and "Bank Deposit".

discounts.description: Discounts backed by discount Functions of the app.

functions.description: The settings of the other Functions, by the handle of the Function.

extensions.description:
What the merchant filled in for the UI extensions of the app, by the handle of the
extension: the values its `shopify.settings` (`useSettings`) reads.

tax_rate.description:
Tax in percent, added on top of the discounted subtotal: `20` for 20 %. No tax when
omitted.

CheckoutShippingRateInput.description: A delivery option the local checkout offers to every address.

handle.description: What Functions and the page call the option: `"standard"`.

title.description: What the buyer sees. Defaults to the handle.

Money.description: An amount of money: an integer number of cents (`1999`, the unit Liquid uses) or a decimal string in the shop currency (`"19.99"`). Floats such as `19.99` are rejected because they are ambiguous.

anyOf.description: Cents, e.g. 1999 for 19.99.
Decimal amount, e.g. "19.99" or "20".

CheckoutDeliveryKind.description: What kind of delivery a shipping rate is.

CheckoutPaymentMethodInput.description: A payment method the local checkout offers.

handle.description: What payment customization Functions and the page call the method: `"card"`.

name.description: What the buyer sees. Defaults to the handle.

placements.description:
Where the method is offered, which payment customization Functions read as
`placements`. Defaults to `["PAYMENT_METHOD"]`: the list of the checkout.

CheckoutPaymentPlacement.description: Where a payment method is offered.

oneOf.description: The list of payment methods of the checkout.
The express buttons (Shop Pay, Apple Pay, ...).

CheckoutDiscountInput.description: A discount backed by a discount Function of the app.

id.description:
The number of the discount's id, which its Function reads
(`gid://shopify/DiscountAutomaticNode/<id>`, or `DiscountCodeNode` with a code) and the
Admin API gives it. Defaults to its position in the list, from 1.

function.description: The handle of the discount Function in the app.

title.description: What the buyer sees. Defaults to the handle of the Function.

code.description: The code that triggers the discount. Without one the discount is automatic.

classes.description: What the discount may reduce. All three when omitted.

metafields.description:
The metafields of the discount, which its Function's input query reads, by
`"namespace.key"`: `{"$app.function-configuration": {"type": "json", "value":
{"percentage": 10}}}` for `metafield(namespace: "$app", key: "function-configuration")`.
Shopify's list of `{namespace, key, type, value}` is taken too.

OwnerMetafields.description:
The metafields of a discount or of the owner of a Function: by `"namespace.key"`, or as
Shopify's Admin API takes them (`metafieldsSet`, `discountAutomaticAppCreate`), a list of
`{namespace, key, type, value}`.

anyOf.description: `{"$app.function-configuration": {"type": "json", "value": {…}}}`.
`[{"namespace": "$app", "key": "function-configuration", "type": "json", "value": {…}}]`.

MetafieldInput.description:
A metafield value. Write the value directly and its type is inferred (string →
`single_line_text_field`, integer → `number_integer`, decimal → `number_decimal`, boolean →
`boolean`, anything else → `json`), or spell out `{"type": ..., "value": ...}`.

TypedMetafield.description: A metafield with an explicit type.

type.description:
A Shopify metafield type, e.g. `single_line_text_field`, `multi_line_text_field`,
`rich_text_field`, `number_integer`, `number_decimal`, `boolean`, `color`, `date`,
`date_time`, `url`, `json`, `money`, `rating`, `weight`, `volume`, `dimension` and the
other measurements (`distance`, `temperature`, `duration`...), `product_reference`,
`collection_reference`, `page_reference`, `article_reference` (`blog/article`, or the
article's handle alone), `file_reference`, `metaobject_reference`, or a `list.` variant
of those.

value.description:
The value. References are written as handles (`"blue-shirt"`), files as paths inside
`files/`, lists as JSON arrays.

OwnerMetafield.description: A metafield as Shopify's Admin API takes it.

type.description:
The metafield type: `json`, `single_line_text_field`, … Inferred from the value when
omitted.

value.description: The value: JSON, or the text Shopify stores (`"{\"percentage\":10}"` for `json`).

CheckoutFunctionInput.description:
A Function that is not a discount (cart transform, delivery or payment customization,
validation): its owner in the shop, and its settings.

enabled.description:
Whether the shop has an owner of the Function (the payment or delivery customization,
validation or cart transform an app creates for it), and it is enabled. As on Shopify,
the Function runs at the checkout only through an enabled owner: `true` runs it, `false`
is an owner that is turned off. Without it, the shop has no owner of it, as after an
install: the Function runs only for a scenario that names it in `extensions`, or for
`app function run <handle>`, with these metafields.

metafields.description:
The metafields of the object the Function belongs to, by `"namespace.key"`:
`{"$app.function-configuration": {"type": "json", "value": {…}}}` for
`metafield(namespace: "$app", key: "function-configuration")`. Shopify's list of
`{namespace, key, type, value}` is taken too.

CheckoutExtensionInput.description: A checkout or customer account UI extension of the app, as the merchant set it up.

settings.description:
The values of the fields of its `[extensions.settings]`, by `key`, as the merchant fills
them in the checkout editor: `{"title": "Free gift", "threshold": 50, "show": true}`. A
field left out has no value (`undefined`), as on Shopify.

ScenarioLook.description: The look of the checkout page.

oneOf.description: The look of the Shop app and Shop Pay.

ScenarioExpectInput.description:
What the checkout of a scenario must look like once its Functions ran, which
`lsf app check` checks. Each list (`payment_methods`, `express_methods`, `delivery_options`,
`discounts`, `lines`, `errors`) takes `includes`, `excludes` and `equals`; `totals` takes
exact amounts:

```json
"expect": {
  "express_methods": { "excludes": ["paypal"] },
  "payment_methods": { "includes": ["paypal"] },
  "totals": { "total": "120.00" }
}
```

step.description:
The step of the buyer journey the Functions run for: `completion` (the default), the
order being placed, as `lsf app function run` runs them; `interaction`, the page as the
buyer sees it before. Only a validation Function tells them apart
(`buyerJourney.step`).

payment_methods.description:
The payment methods of the list of the checkout (`PAYMENT_METHOD`), in order, once the
payment customizations ran. A string matches the handle or the name.

express_methods.description:
The express buttons (`ACCELERATED_CHECKOUT`), in order, once the payment customizations
ran. A method can be in both lists. A string matches the handle or the name.

delivery_options.description:
The delivery options, in the order the buyer sees them, once the delivery customizations
and the shipping discounts ran. A string matches the handle or the title.

discounts.description:
The discounts applied, product, order and shipping ones. A string matches the title (the
message the Function gave) or the code.

lines.description:
The lines of the checkout once the cart transforms ran. A string matches the SKU or the
title.

errors.description:
The errors that block the order: those validation Functions report, and those of
Functions that failed. A string matches the message. `{"equals": []}`: no error.

totals.description: The amounts of the checkout, each exactly.

ScenarioStep.description: The step of the buyer journey the Functions run for.

oneOf.description: The buyer is on the page (`CHECKOUT_INTERACTION`).

includes.description: Each of these matches an entry of the list, in any order.

items.description: An entry of a list of `expect`: its name, or the fields it must have.

anyOf.description: What the entry is named by (see the list).
The fields the entry must have; those left out can be anything.

excludes.description: None of these matches an entry of the list.
